issues.title: [Fix] diffusion: pipeline and model-helper bug fixes
issues.body:
Part of #43875 (items 26-33). Split out of #43585 so it can be reviewed on its own. It does not depend on the other two PRs (#43585, #44887).

Item 25 (Plucker rays in float32 for LingBot-World) moved to its own PR, as asked in review, so it can get a GPU check without holding these up.

## Summary
Fixes in pipelines and the model helpers they use. Item numbers match #43875.

26. The blank default texture and the bake buffers used `(width, height)` where `(height, width)` is needed, which breaks non-square textures.
27. `ImageProcessorV2.load_image` raised `UnboundLocalError` for an ndarray or tensor. ndarrays are handled like PIL images and other types raise a `TypeError`.
28. `DiffusersPipeline` output layout: NumPy videos were permuted twice, a nested PIL list kept only the first video, and several images from an image pipeline were stacked as video frames. A nested list is now stacked to `(B, T, C, H, W)` for every video.
29. `DiffusersPipeline.add_stage` took its arguments in the reverse order of the base class. It now swaps the legacy order and delegates to `ComposedPipelineBase.add_stage`, so it also gets the disagg role filtering.
30. SANA-Video always encoded the negative prompt at 300 tokens. It uses `max_sequence_length` now.
31. ErnieImage treated a `[null, null]` `pe` entry as a real prompt-enhancement model. It is treated as absent.
32. HunyuanImage3 ignored `--revision` when downloading weights.
33. Hunyuan3D picked an arbitrary checkpoint when several matched the fallback glob. It picks the first by name now.

## Tests
- New `test_pipeline_regressions.py` (CPU): 12 cases. The layout test uses distinct values per sample, frame and channel, so swapped axes or a dropped video fail. The ndarray case compares against the same image given as PIL.
- With the source changes reverted, 10 fail. The 2 that still pass are guards: a real Ernie `pe` entry is still detected, and the legacy `add_stage` order still works.
- Unit tests that import the touched modules (25 files) on CPU, PR vs base: 590 passed vs 578 on base. The same 5 failures and 4 GPU-only collection errors occur on base too.
- No tests for 32 and 33 (a passed-through kwarg and a sort). No GPU run; these are API, shape and loading fixes.

issues.title: [Feat] diffusion/openai: Cancel video jobs on DELETE
issues.body:
## Motivation

`DELETE /v1/videos/{id}` removes the job record, but the job keeps its GPU until it finishes (`# TODO: support aborting a job`). A client that cancels a long video job still blocks the replica for the full run.

This revives #24547 by @qimcis, which was approved but no longer applies to main, with a smaller scope:

- a queued job does not start;
- a running job stops after its current denoising step.

Removing one cancelled request from a running dynamic batch is left for a follow-up.

## Modifications

**Cancel channel.** A replica driver runs the forward on the thread that reads its request socket, so it cannot read a cancel while a job runs. The HTTP server now publishes each cancelled request id on a ZMQ PUB socket (`entrypoints/openai/video_cancel.py`). This is the reverse of the progress channel from #45919, with the same deployment limits (monolithic, single node). Each driver subscribes and reads the ids at each check (`managers/request_cancel.py`).

**All ranks stop at the same step.** The driver broadcasts its decision on the replica CPU (gloo) group. In #24547 each rank checked a marker file on its own, so with sequence parallelism one rank could stop at step k while the others waited in a collective of step k+1. The broadcast runs on the CPU group, so it adds no GPU sync.

**Check points.**
- Before the forward in `GPUWorker`, so a queued job never starts.
- After each denoising step, through `PipelineStage.progress_bar`. Every denoising loop advances it once per step, so no loop needs its own edit. Stages that run on the main rank only get no step check, because the check is a collective.
- The sequential path (multi-output SANA-Video 2.0 jobs, and native grouped requests) runs the first stage once for the group. There the worker checks each request before the group starts and runs only the requests that are not cancelled, so each request keeps its own output. The executor also checks before each output, so after a cancel the outputs that remain stop at once.

**DELETE after a timeout.** DELETE publishes the cancel for each job that it removes, also for a job that `--scheduler-rpc-timeout` marked failed: the timeout ends the HTTP wait, not the GPU work. The listener keeps a bounded set of ids, so a cancel for a finished job costs nothing.

**Dynamic batches.** A merged batch is cancellable only when each member is, and it stops only when each member is cancelled. The other members continue. The scheduler checks `OutputBatch.cancelled` before `OutputBatch.error`, in the merged batch and in the native grouped batch, so a stopped batch returns cancelled outputs, not errors.

**Logs.** A cancelled request is logged once at info level (`Stopped request ...`). It is not logged as an error with a traceback on each rank. `OutputBatch.cancelled` lets the HTTP side tell a cancel from a failure. `RequestCancelledError` is in the leaf module `request_cancel_error`, so the logging and profiling utilities import it at module level.

The docs for `DELETE /v1/videos/{id}` are updated.

## Accuracy Tests

Not applicable: the change does not touch model outputs.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

A request that is not cancellable (every request except `/v1/videos` jobs, and every warmup) takes no new path. For a video job, each denoising step adds one non-blocking ZMQ read on the driver and, on a multi-rank replica, one broadcast of one int32 on the gloo CPU group.

Microbenchmark of the per-step check on CPU (Apple M5 Pro, Python 3.14, torch 2.14, 5000 iterations after 500 warmup iterations; local processes over loopback):

| Per-step work | mean | p50 | p99 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `CancelListener.is_cancelled`, no cancel received | 15 us | 16 us | 25 us |
| gloo broadcast of one int32, 2 ranks | 51 us | 49 us | 97 us |
| gloo broadcast of one int32, 4 ranks | 80 us | 76 us | 151 us |
| gloo broadcast of one int32, 8 ranks | 149 us | 146 us | 238 us |

With 8 ranks the check adds about 0.17 ms per step: 0.02 percent of a 1 s MiniMax-H3 step, 0.3 percent of a 50 ms step. The broadcast also makes the CPU thread of each rank wait for the driver once per step, so no rank can queue more than one step of kernels ahead of the driver. A replica across nodes pays the TCP round trip instead of loopback. I did not measure an end-to-end step time before and after on GPU. In the GPU test below, an 8-step MiniMax-H3 job took 9 s with the change. If a maintainer prefers, the check can run every N steps; it cannot use a time interval, because every rank must call the broadcast at the same step.

## Test

**Unit tests** (`test/unit/test_request_cancel.py`, CPU):
- publisher to listener over ipc, ids of expanded outputs (`job:0`), the size bound of the id set;
- a two-process gloo test: every rank follows the driver's decision, also when its own view differs (this test fails when the broadcast is removed);
- the step check stops a loop through `ReportingTqdm`, and only replicated stages get the check;
- the worker skips the forward of a cancelled request;
- the sequential path: a cancelled request does not start and the other requests keep their outputs, the outputs after a cancel stop at once without an error log, and a merged multi-output result stays cancelled;
- DELETE publishes the cancel, also after a scheduler RPC timeout, and a deleted job is not marked failed;
- the dynamic-batch merge rule, and a stopped merged or native grouped batch returns cancelled outputs with no error log;
- `init_request_cancel`, `cancel_endpoint`, and the lifespan start and stop of the publisher;
- each new module imports first without an import cycle.

**GPU test** (covers the per-step and queued checks, not the sequential path; MiniMax-H3 ref2va, 8 x H100, `--ulysses-degree 8 --quantization fp8`, this branch over `lmsysorg/sglang:nightly-dev-20261026`):

| Case | Result |
| --- | --- |
| DELETE a running 50-step job at 10 percent | All 8 ranks stopped after step 6. The next job started 1.1 s after the DELETE and completed. |
| DELETE a job queued behind another job | It never ran. The next job started 1.0 s after the job ahead of it ended. |
| `/health` after the cancels | 200, no NCCL errors |
| Server log after startup | 0 tracebacks, 0 error lines |

## Limits

- A model whose denoising loop does not advance a progress bar runs to the end after a DELETE.
- Stages after denoising (for example decoding) do not run for a cancelled job. A job deleted after its last denoising step still decodes and saves or uploads its output, but the API does not return it.
- Cancellation is best effort: a replica driver that is not connected when the id is published does not receive it.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

issues.title: [Diffusion] Preserve mapped component weights during low-memory offload
issues.body:
## Motivation

Component offload (`--component-residency <c>=component-offload`, and the legacy
`--*-cpu-offload` flags) swapped a component out with
`module.to("cpu", non_blocking=True)` — a full device-to-host copy of **immutable**
weights into fresh host memory on every single swap-out. Three problems this PR removes:

1. **A wasted D2H copy per swap-out.** Inference never mutates weights. Measured on
   MiniMax-H3's 9.7 GiB video VAE on an RTX 5090: 4.85 s on the first cycle, 0.37 s per
   cycle after; now ~0 (one device sync + a pointer rebind).
2. **Unbudgeted, kernel-locked host memory.** `module.to("cpu", non_blocking=True)`
   allocates a *pinned* destination, entirely behind `HostPinBudget`'s back — 9.7 GiB per
   offloaded VAE that the kernel can never reclaim, RssAnon never shows, and no
   accounting ever sees. Pinned offload memory now goes through the budget, and a denial
   degrades to the existing pageable storage without copying anything.
3. **`keep_checkpoint_mapped` weights were destroyed after one use.** A VAE loaded as
   mmap views into its safetensors file (so a constrained host keeps those bytes
   evictable) lost the mapping permanently on the first GPU round trip. The mapping now
   survives: a mapped weight's host copy *is* its mmap view, never replaced.

## Modifications

Five commits:

1. **BCG × offloaded-DiT guard** (`runtime/server_args/server_args.py`). Any explicitly
   non-resident DiT placement with `--enable-breakable-cuda-graph` fails at startup
   validation, next to the other BCG rules: BCG captures the DiT forward, every offload
   flavor rebinds or frees its weight storage between forwards, and a captured graph
   replays capture-time addresses. An auto-selected placement disables BCG with a
   warning; non-DiT components stay free to offload.
2. **Pin-budget divisor** (`runtime/managers/memory_managers/host_memory_budget.py`).
   `HostPinBudget` divides by the node-local worker count (`num_gpus // nnodes`) so N
   ranks stop booking the same host headroom N times; the reserve is taken from the
   per-rank share. A denial degrades to pageable hosting, while the overcommit it
   prevents ends in unreclaimable pinned memory and the OOM killer. Single-GPU
   deployments are unaffected.
3. **Dead-line removal** in `layerwise_offload._ensure_mapped_courier`.
4. **Regression test**: a component-offload GPU round trip must preserve the checkpoint
   mapping (fails on the old strategy, flipped by the next commit).
5. **The host-store rewrite**
   (`runtime/managers/memory_managers/component_residency_strategies.py`). Adopts
   layerwise offload's own storage model at component granularity: a
   `ComponentHostStore` captures the checkpoint-time host weights once (mmap views stay
   mmap views; the rest is pinned within a `HostPinBudget` grant, falling back to
   pageable when the budget declines) and hangs off the module. Swap-in copies
   host-to-device on the prefetch stream and rebinds via `.data`; swap-out rebinds every
   parameter to a shared one-element device placeholder — exactly a released layerwise
   layer, so no D2H copy and no new host allocation, ever. The store survives
   strategy-cache rebuilds, releases its device copy on sleep, and stays coherent with
   writers through the layerwise contracts: weight refits route through
   `update_host_weights` (the `update_cpu_weights` analog) and LoRA merge/unmerge wraps
   mutation in `begin`/`end_host_update`, which re-resolves targets after layer
   replacement. The residency report walks the store like `layerwise_offload_managers`.
   DTensor components work through the same `to_local_tensor`/`wrap_for_target` helpers
   layerwise uses. MPS and FSDP routing are unchanged.

## Accuracy Tests

No numerics change — the same weight bytes reach the device; only where they rest and how
they travel changes. End-to-end MiniMax-H3 (fl2va t2va, 672x384/4 s/8 steps, cookbook
5090 flags with `video_vae=component-offload`, 3 consecutive requests per side) produced
identical outputs on old and new sides.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Component offload is a cookbook-recommended placement for encoder/VAE-sized components.
The real 9.7 GiB H3 video-VAE checkpoint (mmap-loaded, `assign=True`) driven through
`ComponentOffloadStrategy` prepare/finish cycles on a 1× RTX 5090 (32 GB):

| per swap cycle | old strategy | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| swap-out wall | 4.85 s first, 0.37 s after (full D2H) | **~0 s** (sync + rebind) |
| swap-in wall (steady) | 0.37 s (from its pinned copy) | 0.56 s (straight from the mapping) |
| host state at rest | 9.7 GiB **pinned**, unbudgeted; mapping destroyed | 9.7 GiB **still checkpoint-mapped**; zero committed host bytes |
| device bytes per swap-in | 9.71 GiB | 9.71 GiB |

The mapped host copy trades ~0.2 s of swap-in against holding zero committed host
memory; weights the budget grants pinning keep the pinned fast path on both directions.
End-to-end H3 latency is neutral to within noise — the change is memory correctness, not
a latency claim.

Notes:
- `text_encoder=component-offload` cannot work on a 32 GB card for H3 (66.7 GB bf16
  encoder; whole-module swap-in OOMs — verified empirically). The cookbook's layerwise
  placement for it is the right one.
- 5 tests under `test/unit/realtime/`, `test/unit/sana_wm/`, and
  `test_consistency_metrics.py` fail on origin/main, unrelated to this PR; the companion
  `diffusion-fix-unit-tests` branch fixes them separately.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). (One case per failure mode: the keep-mapped round trip; residency buckets stable across swap cycles with values intact; budget denial degrades without copying; both writer paths reach the host store; the BCG guard's raise/disable/ignore cases; the N-rank budget divisor and per-rank-share reserve. Full `multimodal_gen/test/unit` on the 5090 is green except the 5 pre-existing main failures fixed in the companion branch — both together: 2191 passed, 0 failed.)
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). (No flag semantics change; existing docs remain accurate.)
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). (See the sections above.)
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

issues.title: [Diffusion] Cache static text conditioning per request (Krea2 first)
issues.body:
## Motivation

Text conditioning in several multimodal_gen DiTs is recomputed on every denoising step even though it only depends on the prompt and the weights. Helios already caches this per request on `forward_batch.extra`. This PR lifts that helper into `BaseDiT` and applies it to Krea2 first. Draft: the rest of the call sites and GPU numbers are still to do (checklist below).

## Modifications

- `dits/base.py`: move `_request_cache` / `_tensor_key` from Helios into `BaseDiT` so any DiT can reuse them. Helios behavior is unchanged.
- `dits/krea2.py`: `text_fusion` + `txt_in` output is computed once per request and reused on later steps.
- `test_krea2_fp8.py`: one test covering reuse within a request, pos/neg CFG kept separate, and no reuse across requests.

Cache key and lifetime:
- Key is tensor identity (data_ptr, shape, stride, dtype, device) of the context and the text mask.
- The cache lives in `Req.extra`, so it is dropped with the request. Weight updates and LoRA changes happen between requests, so they always start from an empty cache.
- The cached entry holds a reference to its inputs so their data_ptr cannot be reused for another tensor within the request.
- Disabled when there is no forward context or when grad is enabled.

## Checklist before ready for review

Unit tests (CPU)

GPU validation (main vs this branch, same checkpoint, seed, resolution, steps)

- [ ] Confirm the cache actually hits on the real model (one compute per prompt per request)

- [ ] Peak memory delta
- [ ] Same correctness + perf checks for each additional model added

PR hygiene

issues.title: [Perf] diffusion: Remove per-step host syncs and uploads in video models
issues.body:
Depends on #46045 (host-sync guards in `test/unit/host_sync_guard.py`); this branch is stacked on it.

## Motivation

Video pipelines run long denoising loops where every blocking host read or pageable upload stalls the host on the previous step's kernels, and several of them rebuilt request-constant RoPE tables or masks on every forward. This PR removes those per-step costs model by model. Outputs are bitwise unchanged.

## Modifications

- **MOVA** (`model_specific_stages/mova.py`, `bridges/mova_dual_tower.py`): the loop uploaded both timesteps every step and `step_from_to` read them back with `float()`, four syncs per step. The paired schedule is uploaded once and the scheduler steps on the host values. Every forward re-uploaded both towers' CPU complex128 RoPE tables (six blocking copies, ~17 MB for audio) and redid the full-sequence concats, and every bridge layer rebuilt its fp32 cos/sin caches (30 layers x 2 directions); tables and bridge caches are built once per request and freed when the loop ends.
- **MiniMax-H3 / FastH3** (`dits/minimax_h3.py`, `minimax_h3_adaln_cache.py`): FastH3 PDD heads copied that step's weight and bias from the host stacks, four blocking copies per step; the stacks are uploaded once per (device, dtype) and indexed by step. The AdaLN online cache indexed its slabs with a 0-dim device slot (a host read, two per step); it now gathers with `index_select` and keeps the old strides.
- **HunyuanVideo** (`dits/hunyuanvideo.py`): the forward built the RoPE cos/sin on the host and copied both to the device every forward (~59 MB per step at 720p x 125 frames). The uploaded tables are kept per request in an underscore `Req.extra` key, which the disaggregation transport skips.
- **Helios** (`helios_denoising.py`, `dits/helios.py`): frame indices were built on the host and uploaded by each of four RoPE embeddings per forward (eight syncs per CFG step); they are built on the latent device. Every block cast the full-sequence [B, L, 6, D] modulation to fp32 (~1.4 GB per block at 384x640); the compact rows are cast once before the expand/concat.
- **Wan family** (`dits/causal_wanvideo.py`, `dits/wanvideo.py`): causal Wan (LongLive2) copied its host RoPE tables to the device every forward; they are uploaded once per request and chunk position. Wan and causal Wan blocks each cast the batch-wide modulation to fp32; the forward casts it once (the per-token TI2V table keeps its fused bf16 path).
- **LTX-2** (`dits/ltx_2.py`, `ltx_2/denoising.py`; paths not touched by #45966): `prepare_video_coords` uploaded two constant tensors per call (every forward on the LTX-2.3 one-stage path, every step for JoyEcho memory coords); they are uploaded once per device. HQ res2s: the SDE coefficient NaN replacement went through a 0-dim boolean index (nonzero on get and set, four calls per step) and is now a `torch.where`; the 100-iteration bongmath refinement hoists its fp64 casts and `h * a21`; the stage-1 step size starts from the step's host sigmas instead of `.cpu()` reads.
- **JoyEcho** (`joy_echo/denoising.py`): every DMD step read sigma and sigma_next with `.item()`; the loop takes fp32 host and device copies of the schedule once. With the memory bank (shot >= 2) the shot-constant cross masks, audio block mask and memory RoPE coords are built once per loop instead of every step.
- **SANA-WM / SANA-Video2** (`sana_wm*.py`, `sana_wm/streaming*.py`, `sana_video2.py`): the cache-type flag was uploaded in every block's clean pass and read back by the next chunk (20 uploads + 20 reads per chunk) and is now a host tensor; self-forcing steps read their timestep once per chunk; `forward_long` windows camera/Plucker inputs once per chunk so the UCPE and Plucker caches hit; the UCPE invalid-ray fix is a `torch.where`; the chunked refiner reads its sigmas from a host copy and builds each block's RoPE once on the device. SANA-Video2 builds its RoPE tables once per latent shape instead of uploading complex128 tables twice per forward.
- **Cosmos3 world models** (`dits/cosmos_dreams.py`, `dits/cosmos3_sim_auto.py`, `cosmos3_simulation/sim_auto.py`): Dreams zeroed null-action V slots by indexing with a Python list in each of 36 layers (a blocking upload each); the slots are per-frame slices. Sim-Auto's scatter/gather indexes, mRoPE frame ids and generated-frame masks are built once per chunk on the device. The default Cosmos3 T2V/I2V loop is untouched (#45967 covers its CFG window).

Tests:
- `test_mova_denoising.py`: steps never upload or read device timesteps (`SyncOnRead` schedule, one upload); RoPE tables built once per request; outputs bitwise equal.
- `test_minimax_h3_pdd_offline.py`, `test_minimax_h3_adaln_cache.py`: heads uploaded once; slab gathers run under `forbid_host_syncs` with the old values and strides.
- `test_hunyuanvideo_rope_upload.py`, `test_wan_step_host_overhead.py`: RoPE tables uploaded once per request (per chunk position for causal Wan), identical tables; blocks receive fp32 modulation.
- `test_helios_step_host_overhead.py`: frame indices live on the latent device; blocks receive fp32 modulation.
- `test_ltx2_step_host_overhead.py`: video-coord constants uploaded once; SDE coefficients under `forbid_host_syncs`; the refinement casts once.
- `test_joy_echo_denoising_host_overhead.py`: host/device sigma copies, steps never read device sigmas, the memory prefix is built once.

issues.title: [Feat] diffusion: Native SANA-Sprint support
issues.body:
## Motivation

Closes #43671. Joint work with @raghulchandramouli, who independently found the SANA 1.5 qk_norm bug on #43671; his commits are listed under *Joint contributions*.

[SANA-Sprint 0.6B](https://huggingface.co/Efficient-Large-Model/Sana_Sprint_0.6B_1024px_diffusers) is a guidance-distilled SANA variant that generates 1024px images in 1–4 steps. Its checkpoint declares `SanaSprintPipeline` and `SCMScheduler`, and neither had a native implementation. This reuses the SANA transformer, Gemma2 encoder and DC-AE, and adds Sprint's pipeline, scheduler and defaults.

## Modifications

- **`SCMScheduler`** (`runtime/models/schedulers/scheduling_scm.py`): subclasses Diffusers' TrigFlow sCM scheduler. Diffusers' `SanaSprintPipeline` does three things inline in its loop: it rescales the DiT input, converts the DiT's flow prediction to TrigFlow, and divides the final sample by `sigma_data`. Here `scale_model_input` / `step` / `init_noise_sigma` do that work, so the shared `DenoisingStage` loop runs Sprint unchanged. `timesteps` holds the sCM timesteps the DiT is conditioned on. The 2-step intermediate angle (1.3) is applied only for 2 steps, so 1/3/4 steps work without passing `intermediate_timesteps=None` as Diffusers requires.
- **SANA DiT** (`runtime/models/dits/sana.py`):
  - `guidance_embeds` checkpoints get `SanaCombinedTimestepGuidanceEmbeddings`, with Diffusers' module layout and weight names.
  - `qk_norm="rms_norm_across_heads"` is now applied in both the linear self-attention and the cross-attention.
  - The arch default for `qk_norm` changes to `None`, matching Diffusers. SANA 1.0 configs omit the key and have no norm weights.
- **Pipeline** (`runtime/pipelines/sana_sprint.py`, `configs/pipeline_configs/sana_sprint.py`, `configs/sample/sana_sprint.py`):
  - Sprint's "complex human instruction" prompt prefix. It reuses SANA-Video's text stage; the instruction is now a class attribute there, and SANA-Video's behavior is unchanged.
  - Per-request embedded guidance: `guidance_scale × guidance_embeds_scale`, rounded to the DiT dtype as Diffusers does.
  - fp32 latents.
  - Defaults: 2 steps, `guidance_scale=4.5`. CFG never runs, so negative prompts are ignored.
  - **Resolution binning**, on by default as in Diffusers (`use_resolution_binning`). The DiT runs at the closest 1024px aspect-ratio bin, then a Sprint decoding stage resizes and center-crops the image back to the requested size. The bin table copies Diffusers' `ASPECT_RATIO_1024_BIN`: importing it pulls in the whole PixArt pipeline (about 8.5 s), so a unit test asserts the copy still matches.
  - **Schedule overrides** per request: `max_timesteps`, `intermediate_timesteps` and explicit `trigflow_timesteps` (`num_inference_steps + 1` decreasing angles). They are validated at admission (a bad schedule returns HTTP 400: angles must lie in [0, 1.5708], explicit schedules must end at 0, and an explicit `intermediate_timesteps` applies only to 2 steps) and declared in `image_request_extra_fields`, so the image API forwards them. Diffusers 0.37's own custom-`timesteps` path raises a `TypeError`, because `retrieve_timesteps` omits `num_inference_steps` for `SCMScheduler`, so explicit angles are checked against Diffusers' scheduler directly.
  - The SANA detector excludes Sprint ids, and `sana_sprint` registers before generic SANA.
- **Tests:**
  - `test/unit/test_sana_sprint.py` (CPU).
  - 1-GPU server cases `sana_sprint_0.6b_t2i` and `sana_sprint_1.6b_t2i` with component accuracy enabled. Perf and consistency checks are off, as for `sana_video_2b_t2v`.
  - A component-accuracy hook branch: Sprint's DiT takes the same guidance value as Diffusers, not the FLUX-style ×1000.
- **Component-accuracy harness fix** (`component_accuracy/utils.py`): `normalize_state_key` rewrites `scale` to `weight`, which turned DC-AE's `to_qkv_multiscale.*` into `to_qkv_multiweight.*`. Prefix-stripped and suffix candidates were built only from that rewritten name, so 36 of 375 VAE parameters never transferred and any DC-AE case failed at 90.4% matched. Candidates are now derived from the original name too; when the two names are equal, the candidate order is unchanged.
- **Docs:** SANA-Sprint entry in the model catalog.

### Side effect: SANA 1.5 now loads its QK-norm weights

SANA 1.5 checkpoints ship trained `attn1/attn2.norm_q/norm_k` weights in every block. sglang's SANA DiT had no such parameters, so the loader skipped those weights with a warning and served the model without QK-norm. With this PR they load. DiT output against Diffusers' `SanaTransformer2DModel` on `SANA1.5_1.6B_1024px_diffusers` (real weights, fixed random inputs, bf16):

| | `norm_q`/`norm_k` params | rel. L2 vs Diffusers | cosine |
|---|---|---|---|
| upstream main | 0 | 25.0% | 0.969 |
| this PR | 80 | 3.5% | 0.9994 |

SANA 1.0 (600M / 1600M) is unaffected: no `qk_norm` in config, so no norm modules are built.

### Joint contributions from raghulchandramouli

- **SANA-Sprint 1.6B** (`Sana_Sprint_1.6B_1024px_diffusers`) is registered by exact id next to 0.6B, in the registry, the registry test and the model catalog. Its configs differ from 0.6B only in transformer size.
- **`test/unit/test_sana_dit_param_names.py`** (CPU) builds the native and Diffusers DiTs on the meta device for six real configs (SANA 1.0 600M/1600M, SANA 1.5 1.6B/4.8B, Sprint 0.6B/1.6B) and runs the loader's own name mapping. It asserts that every checkpoint weight lands on a native parameter of the same shape, and that no native parameter is left unloaded. Against main's DiT, the four configs with qk_norm or guidance embeddings fail; SANA 1.0 passes.
- **Scheduler review and schedule validation fixes.** Out-of-range TrigFlow angles used to reach the DiT (for example, `max_timesteps=2.3562` gave a timestep of about -9e4) and are now rejected at admission. An explicit `intermediate_timesteps` with steps other than 2 used to be dropped silently and is now rejected, as in Diffusers. The review also led to the `pred_original_sample` note in `SCMScheduler.step`'s docstring.

## Test

**Scheduler:** `test_scm_scheduler_reproduces_diffusers_sprint_loop` runs a deterministic stand-in for the bf16 DiT through Diffusers' `SanaSprintPipeline` loop and through the shared-loop call order, for 1, 2 and 4 steps. The outputs match bit for bit (`atol=0`). While writing it I caught a dtype issue: a 0-dim fp32 coefficient times a bf16 DiT output stays bf16, which drifted by about 1e-2. The scheduler now upcasts explicitly, and the test fails if that upcast is removed.

**Component accuracy, 0.6B (1-GPU harness):** all three checks pass. Before the harness fix above, the VAE check failed on weight transfer.

| component | CosSim vs Diffusers/HF |
|---|---|
| transformer (with guidance + qk_norm) | 0.999985 |
| text encoder (Gemma2) | 0.999829 |
| VAE (DC-AE) | 0.999781 |

**End to end vs Diffusers, 0.6B** (`SanaSprintPipeline`, bf16 DiT, VAE upcast to fp32 to match sglang). Same seed (42), 1024×1024, `guidance_scale=4.5`, image PSNR:

| prompt | 1 step | 2 steps | 4 steps |
|---|---|---|---|
| a tiny astronaut hatching from an egg on the moon | 37.0 dB | 33.8 dB | 36.9 dB |
| a red fox sitting in fresh snow, golden hour, photorealistic | 37.3 dB | 42.6 dB | 40.3 dB |
| an isometric illustration of a cozy library with plants and warm lamps | 27.4 dB | 27.7 dB | 28.1 dB |

**Resolution binning and schedule overrides vs Diffusers** (fox prompt, seed 42, 2 steps):

| request | output size (sglang = Diffusers) | PSNR |
|---|---|---|
| 1000×700 (bin 1216×832, resized back) | 700×1000 | 39.2 dB |
| 800×1200 | 1200×800 | 33.8 dB |
| 960×640 | 640×960 | 39.2 dB |
| `intermediate_timesteps=1.1` | 1024×1024 | 41.1 dB |

Over HTTP, explicit `trigflow_timesteps=[1.5708, 1.3, 0]` reproduces the default 2-step image bit for bit. A custom 4-angle schedule produces a clean image. A malformed schedule returns 400 with the reason.

The third prompt is the most detailed image; it keeps the same composition, with fine-detail differences. I traced the gap: there is no single divergence point. Each block differs from Diffusers by about 0.3% (bf16 rounding), and the 28 blocks amplify that to about 7% at the output. Diffusers' own bf16 DiT is just as far from its fp32 run:

| DiT input (real, from the pipeline) | Diffusers bf16 vs fp32 | sglang bf16 vs fp32 | sglang vs Diffusers (bf16) |
|---|---|---|---|
| prompt 1 | 5.0% | 5.5% | 3.8% |
| prompt 3 | 10.1% | 10.2% | 6.9% |

So sglang's output is as close to fp32 as Diffusers' bf16 path is. Switching sglang's linear attention to Diffusers' fp32 formulation, or the caption RMSNorm eps to 1e-5, does not reduce the gap.

**Component accuracy, 1.6B** (1-GPU harness, RTX A6000): all three checks pass.

| component | CosSim vs Diffusers/HF |
|---|---|
| transformer (with guidance + qk_norm) | 0.999979 |
| text encoder (Gemma2) | 0.999829 |
| VAE (DC-AE) | 0.999781 |

**End to end vs Diffusers, 1.6B** (same setup as 0.6B), image PSNR:

| prompt | 1 step | 2 steps | 4 steps |
|---|---|---|---|
| a tiny astronaut hatching from an egg on the moon | 30.0 dB | 26.7 dB | 28.3 dB |
| a red fox sitting in fresh snow, golden hour, photorealistic | 26.2 dB | 26.5 dB | 25.3 dB |
| an isometric illustration of a cozy library with plants and warm lamps | 29.0 dB | 26.7 dB | 28.0 dB |

1.6B scores lower than 0.6B, but the images keep the same composition, pose and lighting and differ only in fine texture. Against an fp32 Diffusers reference (`SanaSprintPipeline` in fp32, TF32 off), both bf16 paths land about equally far away, and sglang is never further:

| prompt | sglang bf16 vs fp32 (1 / 2 / 4 steps) | Diffusers bf16 vs fp32 (1 / 2 / 4 steps) |
|---|---|---|
| astronaut | 28.0 / 25.5 / 26.7 dB | 28.0 / 25.5 / 26.3 dB |
| fox | 26.2 / 27.1 / 28.8 dB | 26.7 / 25.4 / 25.3 dB |
| library | 28.0 / 25.9 / 26.9 dB | 28.1 / 25.8 / 26.8 dB |

## Speed Tests and Profiling

RTX A6000, 1024×1024, warm requests (ms, three runs; the first is cold):

| steps | sglang | Diffusers |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 12174 (cold), 655, 623 | 4704 (cold), 640, 685 |
| 2 | 695, 698, 741 | 755, 756, 725 |
| 4 | 895, 1004, 840 | 1020, 933, 955 |

Comparable latency. Sprint is not admitted to Breakable CUDA Graph or other fast paths in this PR. `perf_baselines/h100.json` gets entries for both new cases because the server test requires them, but their numbers (0.6B: load ~61 s, e2e ~11.8 s cold, `estimated_full_test_time_s=108.4`; 1.6B: load ~62 s, e2e ~0.39 s, `estimated_full_test_time_s=86.1`) were measured on the A6000, not an H100. They only feed CI sharding while `run_perf_check=False`, so please regenerate them on H100 if you want an accurate shard estimate.

## Test environment

- GPU: 1× NVIDIA RTX A6000 (48 GB, sm_86), driver 610.43.02
- Host: Ubuntu 22.04.5, 6 vCPU
- Software: Python 3.12.13, torch 2.14.1+cu130, diffusers 0.37.0, transformers 5.19.0, nvcc 13.0.88
- Base: measured on upstream `main` at 363e6c6b4d, then rebased onto 79eb10e182 (the 7 commits in between touch no diffusion code; the Sprint, SANA-Video, registry and harness unit tests re-pass after the rebase)

## Tests run

- `test/unit/test_sana_sprint.py`: 10 passed (14 after the joint commits). They cover the scheduler against Diffusers' Sprint loop, including intermediate-angle and explicit-angle schedules; schedule validation; image-API field forwarding; binning (table, bin choice, latent shape, resize/crop); registry; and the `qk_norm` default. Each case was checked to fail with its targeted change reverted: the bf16 upcast, the `qk_norm` default, the registry priority, binning ignoring its flag, the scheduler ignoring explicit angles, and an undeclared API field.
- `test/unit/test_sana_dit_param_names.py`: 6 passed. This and `test_sana_sprint.py` were re-run on Linux CPU at 527ebc9, after merging main, along with the cfg-warmup and OpenAI image-API unit tests (252 passed).
- Unit tests touching the SANA DiT, SANA-Video stages, registry, OpenAI request helpers, component-accuracy harness, GPU cases or perf baselines: 984 passed.
- `test/server/test_server_1_gpu.py -k sana_sprint`: 2 passed (0.6B and 1.6B). Component accuracy: 3 passed for each of 0.6B and 1.6B.

Not done here:
- **TP/SP.** SANA's DiT has none, and its GLUMBConv feed-forward would need halo exchange to shard spatially. For a 0.6B model running at about 0.7 s per image, it isn't worth it.
- **BCG admission.** I'll do it as a follow-up with the eager-vs-BCG byte-identity and A/B timing evidence that admission requires.
- **CLI flags for the new per-request fields.** The shared sampling parser asks that no model-specific fields be added there. The fields work through the HTTP and Python APIs.
- **Binning for plain SANA.** Diffusers' `SanaPipeline` also bins by default and sglang's SANA does not. That would change existing SANA outputs, so it is left out of this PR.

issues.title: [Fix] diffusion/realtime: Keep frame payloads contiguous
issues.body:
## Motivation

Large realtime frame batches use two WebSocket messages: a MessagePack header
followed by the raw payload. Under send backpressure, the event listener could
insert an error response between them. Clients then interpreted the error as
video data. A failure while generating the next chunk could also cancel the
previous chunk's unfinished send before reporting the error.

## Changes

- Serialize frame output and invalid-event responses with a per-session lock.
- Finish pending output before reporting a subsequent generation error. Client
  disconnect and cancellation retain their existing cancellation paths.
- Extend existing realtime tests; preserve generation/send overlap.
- Correct the SANA-WM cookbook and client example to handle both inline
  `frame_batch` and `frame_batch_header` + binary payload.

No new configuration, output queue, payload copy, or model changes. Production
code changes are limited to two existing files (+15/-10).

## Validation

- Linux realtime suite: **2 failed, 152 passed** before the fix; **154 passed**
  afterward, including on the final head. The protocol regression uses the real
  WebSocket and output adapter with deterministic ASGI send backpressure.
- Real SANA-WM streaming server on **1x H200**, 256x256, 4 steps, seed 42:
  five sessions per revision covering normal completion, invalid events,
  disconnect and reconnect. A test-only 100 ms delay after header writes exposes
  the transport interleaving. Baseline corruption reproduced; with the fix,
  all four invalid-event responses arrived outside frame pairs and video
  payload hashes matched the clean baseline. Health remained HTTP 200.
- The optional refiner was disabled for this lifecycle test. This is not a
  full-quality benchmark, a speedup claim, or proof of failover/long-run HA.
- Pre-commit passes. No new GPU CI job is added.

issues.title: [Perf] diffusion: Keep every component resident in auto mode when memory allows
issues.body:
## Motivation

`--performance-mode auto` places components from a static per-model allowlist. Above `keep_resident_min_available_gb` (the model's value, else 45 GB for image and 120 GB for video models) only `keep_resident_components` stay resident: the VAE by default, plus the DiT for image models. Everything else streams layer by layer at any memory size:
- Z-Image, Ideogram-4, FLUX, Qwen-Image and LTX-2 stream their text encoder even on a 288 GB GPU. A B300 server log reads `267.1 GiB of free device memory selects layerwise offload for text_encoder` and then `resident=0/36`; Z-Image-Turbo spends 0.066 s of a 0.354 s request moving 3.4 GB over PCIe.
- Wan2.2-T2V/I2V-A14B list `auto` in `dit_layerwise_offload_modes` and set no threshold, so both 14B experts stream layer by layer on every GPU, including H200/B200/B300. That also pins ~54 GB of host memory per rank.

On H100, Z-Image-Turbo with every component resident was 12% faster than auto (0.701/0.699 vs 0.793/0.799 s). The memory-aware fix was meant to come from the warmup-calibrated planner (#37917/#37918), which is not merged. This PR adds a conservative interim rule.

## Modifications

- Memory-rich tier in auto mode (`ServerArgsAutoTuner._fits_all_components_resident`): when the least-free selected GPU has at least twice the per-GPU weight bytes free, every component without an explicit placement stays resident. That means no default layerwise list, no DiT layerwise and component offload cleared, which is the placement `speed` mode gives. Explicit placement flags still win per component.
  - Weights are sized before load from the cached checkpoint's safetensors headers (`checkpoint_component_sizes` in `loader/utils.py`): every `model_index.json` component, counted in its serving precision (`resolve_component_precision`, else as stored), with DiT folders divided by `tp_size`. Text encoders count as full copies even when TP-folded, which is conservative.
  - The tier does not apply, and the per-model policy runs as before, when the checkpoint is not fully cached yet, holds non-safetensors or quantized weights, or is overridden (`--quantization`, `--transformer-weights-path`, SVDQuant, component paths, weights or quantizations, model overlays). It also does not apply with dynamic batching (the factor of two assumes one request's activations), on shared host/device memory (GB10) or on MPS.
  - The rule is platform-agnostic. On ROCm, where auto has no layerwise defaults and offloads the text encoder whole, a GPU that fits the rule now keeps it resident too.
- Wan2.2-T2V/I2V-A14B set `keep_resident_min_available_gb=120` with the DiT and VAE resident. Both experts stay on the GPU on H200-class cards and above; 80 GB cards keep streaming (the two bf16 experts alone are 53 GiB). This holds even when the tier cannot size the checkpoint.

What changes on common GPUs (single GPU unless noted; per-GPU weights at serving precision):

| Model | Weights per GPU | Tier at 2x | H100 80 GB (~79 GiB free) | H200 (~139 GiB free) | 32 GB RTX 5090 (~31 GiB free) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Z-Image-Turbo | 19.1 GiB | 38 GiB | all resident (text encoder was layerwise) | all resident | unchanged |
| FLUX.1-dev | 31.4 GiB | 63 GiB | all resident (T5 was layerwise) | all resident | unchanged |
| Qwen-Image-2.1 | 30.2 GiB | 60 GiB | all resident | all resident | unchanged |
| Qwen-Image | 53.7 GiB (TP2: 34.7) | 107 GiB (TP2: 69) | unchanged (TP2: all resident) | all resident | unchanged |
| Cosmos3-Nano | 32.5 GiB | 65 GiB | all resident | all resident | unchanged |
| Wan2.1-T2V-1.3B | 24.3 GiB (fp32 T5) | 49 GiB | all resident | all resident | unchanged |
| LTX-2 | 65.7 GiB | 131 GiB | unchanged | all resident | unchanged |
| Wan2.2-T2V-A14B | 74.9 GiB (fp32 T5) | 150 GiB | unchanged | both experts and VAE resident (threshold), T5 layerwise | unchanged |
| Ideogram-4 FP8, ModelOpt FP8/NVFP4 | not sized (quantized or `--transformer-path`) | | unchanged | unchanged | unchanged |

B200 (178 GiB free) and B300 (288 GiB) fit every bf16 row, Wan2.2-A14B included. Rows other than Z-Image-Turbo and Wan2.2-A14B follow from the sizing rule; they were not run.

Tests:
- `test_server_args.py`: Z-Image-Turbo keeps every component resident at 139 GiB free and at 45 GiB free (the bf16 serving size fits twice there, the fp32-stored bytes would not). 31 and 23 GiB free resolve exactly as an unsized checkpoint does. Batching, shared host/device memory and an unsized checkpoint keep the text encoder layerwise. Off CUDA, the tier replaces the whole-component text-encoder offload. Wan2.2-A14B keeps both experts and the VAE resident at 139 GiB free while T5 streams, and keeps everything resident at 280 GiB free with sizes.
- `test_weight_utils.py::TestCheckpointComponentSizes`: per-component sizes from a local layout and from a cached hub snapshot without network access; a partially downloaded snapshot (only `model_index.json`, as before the worker downloads), a missing shard, `.bin` weights or FP8 weights stay unsized.
- `conftest.mock_cuda_platform` and the server-args helper stub the sizing, so tests that construct `ServerArgs` for a real repo id never read the runner's HF cache.
- Docs: the `auto` row of the performance-mode table in the deployment cookbook describes the tier.

The new tests fail on main: the sizing helper does not exist there, and the all-resident, serving-precision, off-CUDA and Wan2.2 assertions fail on their own.

## Accuracy Tests

Placement only: the same modules run on the same device, so outputs do not change. On 1xH200, Z-Image-Turbo outputs for five distinct prompts have the same md5s on main and this PR.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Z-Image-Turbo on 1xH200, flagless `sglang serve` (auto mode), 1024x1024, 9 steps. Each run: fresh server, 2 warmup requests, then 5 measured requests, each with a distinct prompt so the conditioning cache never answers the text encoder's work. Rounds interleaved main / PR / main / PR:

| | e2e median (round 1 / round 2) | `TextEncodingStage` | Peak memory per request |
|---|---|---|---|
| main (text encoder layerwise) | 0.952 / 0.954 s | 0.130 s | 15,456 MB |
| this PR (all resident) | 0.867 / 0.863 s | 0.031 s | 22,170 MB |

That is −9% end to end. Every PR sample is below every main sample (0.860–0.872 vs 0.950–1.008 s). The server logs `Auto memory policy for ZImagePipelineConfig: 139.3 GiB free on the least-free selected GPU holds the 19.1 GiB of weights per GPU at least 2x, so every component without an explicit placement stays resident.`

The same PR with all but 30 GiB of the GPU held by another process (the inputs of a 32 GB card) keeps main's placement: text encoder and VAE layerwise, DiT component-offloaded, `TextEncodingStage` 0.130 s.

Earlier evidence for the same gap: H100 Z-Image-Turbo, all resident 0.701/0.699 s vs auto 0.793/0.799 s (−12%).

Wan2.2-T2V-A14B, flagless on 1xH200 (startup only; no timed request): main streams both experts (`transformer` and `transformer_2`: 1.74 GB on the GPU, 26.18 GB pinned on the host each) and the text encoder. This PR loads both experts on the GPU (26.62 GB each) and keeps the VAE resident and the fp32 T5 layerwise, so 52 GB less pinned host memory per rank; the tier itself does not apply (150 GiB needed, 139 free). The end-to-end gain was not measured here.

## CI and baselines

The tier changes placement on the 80 GB H100 lanes wherever the checkpoint is cached and fits twice, so these scenarios will report higher `load_peak_vram_mb` / `runtime_peak_vram_mb` and fail the up-only 1%/2% memory checks by design. Their latency baselines may become stale-high (not a failure). Re-seed them with the usual two-step flow (first run prints the blocks to add to `perf_baselines/h100.json`):
- 1 GPU: `flux_image_t2i`, `zimage_image_t2i`, `zimage_image_t2i_multi_lora`, `cosmos3_nano_t2i`, `cosmos3_nano_t2v` (transformer already pinned resident; the small components join it), `sana_video_2b_t2v`, `longlive2_t2v`, `longlive2_i2v`, `fast_hunyuan_video` (38.5 GiB, 77 of ~79 GiB: closest to the line), `wan2_2_ti2v_5b`, `fastwan2_2_ti2v_5b`, `turbo_wan2_1_t2v_1.3b`, and the Wan2.1-T2V-1.3B family (`wan2_1_t2v_1.3b`, `_teacache_enabled`, `_frame_interp_2x`, `_upscaling_4x`, `_frame_interp_2x_upscaling_4x`, `wan2_1_t2v_1_3b_lora_1gpu`).
- 2 GPUs: `flux_image_t2i_2_gpus`, `zimage_image_t2i_2_gpus`, `zimage_image_t2i_2_gpus_non_square`, `qwen_image21_t2i_tp2`, `wan2_1_t2v_1.3b_cfg_parallel`, `wan2_1_t2v_1_3b_cache_dit_sp_only_2gpu`, `fsdp-inference`.
- `wan2_1_t2v_1.3b_encoder_permanent_residents` exists to test a permanent layerwise resident set on the text encoder, so it now pins the encoder layerwise with `--component-residency text_encoder=layerwise-offload`.
- Unchanged: the 5090 lane (nothing fits twice in ~31 GiB), every quantized or `--transformer-path` case, cases with explicit placement of the components that would move, Wan2.2-A14B, Qwen-Image 1-GPU, LTX and MiniMax-H3 on H100. The B200 lane runs only ModelOpt cases with `--transformer-path`/quantized weights.

The list comes from sizing each case's checkpoint at its serving precision against ~79 GiB free; a runner whose HF cache misses a model keeps main's placement for it.

## Risks

- Steady VRAM grows by the components that used to stream (Z-Image-Turbo +6.7 GB peak, the LTX-2 text encoder on H200, ~53 GiB of Wan2.2-A14B experts on H200). The factor of two leaves at least the weights' size free for activations, assuming one request at a time.

issues.title: [Feat] [AMD] diffusion: run Sol-Attn on ROCm gfx1201 with aiter's Sol kernel
issues.body:
> **Draft.** Stacked on #43687 (gfx1201 `AITER_SAGE`), which is stacked on #43686. Depends on the gfx1201 Sol-Attn op in aiter (parts 3-4 of the series: previews Shan2L/aiter#2 HIP kernel, Shan2L/aiter#3 code object), which follows ROCm/aiter#6390. This PR stays a draft until those are merged. Until then the diff includes the commits of the PRs below it; only the last commit belongs to this PR. Overall plan: [ROCm/aiter#6292](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/6292#issuecomment-6106014448).

## Motivation

`SOL_ATTN` (NVlabs Sol-Attn, block-sparse attention with a dense guard for the first steps / layers) is rejected on ROCm, because its only kernel is the CUDA `sol_attn` package. aiter is adding `aiter.gfx1201_sol_attention` for Radeon RDNA4 (gfx1201: Radeon AI PRO R9700 / R9600D, Radeon RX 9070 series). It takes the same arguments as `sol_attn.sol_attn` with `thresh_type="diag"` (per-query-block routing on `tau`, plus sink tokens), and runs Sage-style INT8 QK^T / FP8 PV on the selected blocks.

Independent implementation: `aiter.gfx1201_sol_attention` is our own HIP and AMDGPU assembly implementation of the algorithm published in the Sol-Attn paper ([arXiv 2607.24027](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.24027)). It contains no code from NVlabs/Sana or the `sol_attn` package; it only takes the same arguments. The CUDA path keeps using the `sol_attn` package as before.

## Modifications

- **Platform.** On ROCm, `SOL_ATTN` is selected when the GPU is gfx1201 and the installed aiter provides `gfx1201_sol_attention`. Otherwise it raises an explicit error, as before but with the requirement in the message.
- **Sparse path.** On ROCm, `SolAttnImpl` calls `aiter.gfx1201_sol_attention` with the configured `tau`, `sink_tokens`, `sink_start` and the layer's `softmax_scale`. Only `thresh_type="diag"` is supported (anything else raises); `kv_splits` is a CUDA scheduling knob and is not used.
- **Dense guard.** `dense_backend` gains an `aiter_sage` option, the default on ROCm. It reuses `AITERSageImpl` (so `gfx1201_sage_attention` with #43687), including the packed trailing-padding handling of `forward_varlen`.
- **Import.** `flash_attn_varlen_func` is imported lazily, so the module loads on ROCm.
- **Docs.** `attention_backends.mdx` lists gfx1201 support and the new `dense_backend` value.

CUDA behaviour is unchanged: the default dense backend stays `fa`, and the CUDA path still calls `sol_attn`.

Unit tests are in `test/unit/test_sol_attn_backend.py` and use stubbed `aiter` / platform, so they need no GPU. They cover platform selection and its errors, the arguments passed to `gfx1201_sol_attention`, the `thresh_type` check, and the `aiter_sage` dense guard for `forward` and `forward_varlen`.

## Accuracy and speed

MiniMax-H3, with the case parameters of `minimax_h3_t2va_2gpu_h100`: t2va, 1344x768, 4 s, 8 steps, seed 42, TP2, on 2x R9700 (PyTorch 2.11 / ROCm 7.15), same flags as that case. Sol rows: `--attention-backend sol_attn --attention-backend-config dense_steps=3 --component-attention-backends text_encoder=torch_sdpa,transformer=sol_attn` (default `tau=1.0`, dense layers `0,1`; `dense_steps` lowered from the default 10 because the case has 8 steps). Video PSNR and audio cosine are against the `torch_sdpa` run.

| attention | denoise stage | vs BF16 SDPA | video PSNR / audio cos vs SDPA run |
|---|---|---|---|
| `torch_sdpa` (BF16) | 152.3 s | 1.00x | - |
| `torch_sdpa`, K/V token order reversed (rounding-only noise floor) | 152.3 s | - | 34.41 dB / 0.991 |
| `aiter_sage` (#43687, aiter part 2) | 94.2 s | 1.62x | 32.14 dB / 0.897 |
| `sol_attn`, this PR, aiter part 3 (HIP kernel) | 91.2 s | 1.67x | 32.14 dB / 0.948 |
| `sol_attn`, this PR, aiter part 4 (code object) | 89.4 s | 1.70x | 32.30 dB / 0.946 |

At this short sequence (4 s video), 3 of 8 steps and 2 of 50 layers run dense, so Sol gains little over dense Sage. The sparse kernel pays off at longer sequences and more steps: on the 15 s / 362-frame ref2av case (29 steps) in LightX2V with its shipped MiniMax-H3 Sol config, the same kernels give 211.6 -> 63.7 s (part 3) / 60.8 s (part 4) per DiT step, against 89.1 s for dense Sage (part 2).

The R9700 runs used `sgl-kernel` built for gfx1201 (#43679), and the custom all-reduce was disabled because R9700s connect over PCIe (#43676).

## Checklist

- [x] Format code with pre-commit.
- [x] Add unit tests.
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed results (above).
- [ ] aiter parts 3 and 4 merged; then mark ready for review.

## Summary

Remove unused helpers, write-only state and duplicated implementations:

- USP's obsolete collective wait wrapper and its unused import, NVFP4's unused tensor-shape wrapper, and SVG2's unused kwargs checker.
- Qwen edit's unused condition-image sizing method and Qwen VAE's unused constructor-time convolution counts.
- Old Cache-DiT step-count/warmup fields; mounting still uses the complete active cache key.
- LTX's old LoRA phase field; switching still uses the active phase/strength signature.
- Unused disaggregation configuration copies and RIFE's unused resolved-path field.
- Encoder's unused mapping copy and the unused stage logging setter.
- Empty HF config registry and unreachable config reloading; standard AutoConfig registration remains supported.
- Obsolete disagg_args compatibility shim and its alias-only test; actual role/CLI definitions stay in server_args/disagg.py.
- Share spatial VAE tile geometry across tiled encode/decode and parallel tiled/patch decode, retaining independent traversal, blending and communication.
- Share SLA/SageSLA projection initialization, feature-map setup and reference linear-attention math within the existing backend module; keep sparse kernels separate.
- Share identical TP query/KV head partition rules across Llama, Qwen3, Gemma2 and Gemma3; retain model-specific projections, RoPE, QK norm and sliding attention.
- Reuse the existing linear weight allocator for ConvRot INT8 JIT and comfy backends; keep their validation, scale storage and postprocessing independent.
- Share MOVA audio/video text and time embeddings, time projection and block initialization, preserving registration order and distinct heads/patch convolutions.
- Reuse common sampling request extras for action policies without changing their fields, inheritance or action-specific request merge.
- Share Qwen-Image/JoyImage/Krea2 channelwise VAE decode normalization without changing tensor construction or reciprocal/cast order.
- Share LTX2/SANA-WM video latent normalization in the existing VAE config module.
- Inherit identical CUDA/MUSA unsupported-device methods and the default XPU communicator.
- Reuse identical ModelOpt FP8 inference dispatch while retaining separate postprocessing.
- Reuse the existing unquantized linear weight allocator for embeddings, without changing the embedding method's base class or its apply/embedding implementations.
- Unused diffusion CPU-architecture probe (the SRT implementation remains used and unchanged), plus eight obsolete test-only HTTP/port/memory/video/GT helper functions and their typing-only import.
- Uncalled post-training SP reduce, temporary logger suppression and error-formatting helpers.
- Inline the single-caller AutoConfig wrapper and remove redundant NVFP4 list forwarding.
- Share Wan/LingBot 3D sequence-shard RoPE coordinate construction in the existing NDRotaryEmbedding class, keeping their independent model-level LRU caches.
- Share identical generic/H3 latent input verification in the existing latent-preparation module, preserving H3's inheritance and noise-generation path.
- Unwired function-level Python tracing and its unused env entry. Setting the removed env emits a retirement warning; --enable-trace request tracing is unchanged.
- Superseded CLI cleanup, safetensors shard filtering, single-file NVFP4 wrapper, and unused HF helpers/context-length constant. Active file-selection and quantization paths are unchanged; SRT's same-named utilities are untouched.

- Share H3 positive-finite float validation between sampling configuration and canonical requests through the existing configuration utility module, preserving accepted inputs and error messages.

- Share 2x2 latent packing across Qwen-Image, FLUX.1 and LongCat through the existing pipeline configuration base, removing FLUX's dependency on a private Qwen helper. FLUX.2's distinct layout is unchanged.

- Share Cosmos3's QKV/output projection initialization within its existing model module; causal and cross-attention retain separate head checks, norms and execution paths.

- Reuse the existing prequantized NVFP4 GEMM implementation for the ordinary linear path's duplicated tail, preserving activation quantization, tuple opt-in rejection and output reshape.

- Share SANA-WM AdaLN modulation preparation between dense and streaming block entry points, without merging their attention, cache or FFN control flow.

- Remove thirteen unused parallel-state/communication and WebUI argument helpers. Keep process-group initialization/destruction, active DP accessors and the declared distributed exports unchanged.

- Remove unused LTX2 latent denormalization helpers, Z-Image padding inspection and the obsolete sequence-rank alias. Active decoder normalization and canonical SP accessors remain unchanged.

- Remove superseded capacity-blind disaggregation selection, its unused maximum-slot setting and kwargs plumbing, and the empty completion hook. Capacity-aware selection is now the abstract policy contract; production algorithms, counters, locks and pool routing are unchanged.

- Store disaggregation request start timestamps directly instead of allocating a private dataclass with an unused stage timestamp; preserve exported statistics, locking and formulas. Remove LTX2's unused generic coordinate wrapper while retaining the directly used video/audio methods.

- Remove forward-context batch-size timing that was permanently disabled with no configuration or caller, together with its unused globals/imports and unwritten attention-backend field/setter. Preserve active timestep, metadata, batch and nested-context restoration; request/stage observability is unchanged.

- Remove the unused pipeline JSON-export method and its exclusive imports, plus empty stage hook/offload methods with no callers or overrides. Keep CLI JSON loading and active stage load_model fallback intact.

- Remove MOVA scheduler's uncalled training target/weight and reverse-recovery methods, unused training branch/argument and write-only training state. Retain train_timesteps/train_sigmas because inference step_from_to uses their lookup tables.

- Share the validation and construction logic of MOVA's directional sequential and single-modality pair modes within their existing scheduler method, retaining each direction's tensor operation order and errors.

143 existing production files: net 1,820 lines removed, including the obsolete disaggregation shim. 109 net lines removed from existing test files, including obsolete helper definitions; one stale source reference corrected. No test cases or assertions were removed. No new files, configuration, tests, or numerical-path changes.

- Reuse offload component-name normalization for load ordering; remove its duplicate implementation without changing suffix handling or risk ranking.

- Share identical model unwrapping between Ideogram and Z-Image BCG prompt padders in their existing prompt-padding utility; preserve wrapper lookup order and the separate model-identification semantics.

- Remove six obsolete `channels_last_3d` API-existence checks in VAE loading/layout and parallel convolution. Keep device-policy gates, tensor-layout checks, conversion exceptions, and environment overrides unchanged.

issues.body:
## Motivation and changes

Speed up SANA-Video's residual-gate add on H200 using the **KDA-1.5 + Codex CLI + Kimi K3** candidate. Its transposed residual layout makes the original CUDA implementation expensive; the Triton path tiles along the physical stride-1 token dimension and preserves the original multiply-round-add semantics, output strides, guards, custom-op/fake interface and fallback.

**This PR now changes one production file and retains one kernel family: `residual_gate_add`.** The other 39 families from the earlier version have been removed entirely: any family with a measured regression, or without established material end-to-end benefit, stays at the upstream implementation. No per-shape salvage was used. Existing repository tests are unchanged, and the `kernel-design-agents` coauthor is retained.

Baseline: `c842d32b0ab45753178c5f6420662d7812766aca`. Candidate: `76aa0c6c8db3efd275a250a4b9aa07fd13b23a5a`. All results below were freshly measured with this isolated one-file candidate, so the E2E results are attributable to the retained change. The earlier 40-family combined results are not used as evidence for this revision.

## Kernel validation

NVIDIA H200; three independent processes; CUPTI cold-L2 timing. Speedup is baseline latency / candidate latency. Every original frozen case remains included; two additional actual SANA-Video layouts are reported separately. All measured ratios are at least 1; this is a statement about the tested cases, not a guarantee for arbitrary inputs.

| Workloads | Cases | Three geometric-mean speedups | Worst ratio across all repeats |
|---|---:|---|---:|
| Original frozen suite | 33 | 1.2702× / 1.2686× / 1.2698× | 1.0017× |
| SANA-Video captured layouts | 2 | 2.5418× / 2.5434× / 2.5416× | 2.5385× |

SANA layout: BF16 `[1, 32760, 2240]`, transposed residual/output, contiguous update, broadcast gate with the two captured storage offsets. Latency is approximately **331 μs → 130 μs**. Captured-layout correctness and changed-input prepared calls pass. **35 existing residual-gate tests pass**, including dtype/layout/offset, compile, graph and fallback coverage.

[Raw kernel results](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/blob/42d1d19e5f876e7b5977fb55d90073230bce1655/diffusion-prs/kda-residual-gate-h200-20260927/kernel-benchmarks.json) · [Existing tests](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/blob/42d1d19e5f876e7b5977fb55d90073230bce1655/diffusion-prs/kda-residual-gate-h200-20260927/existing-tests.log) · [KDA provenance](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/blob/42d1d19e5f876e7b5977fb55d90073230bce1655/diffusion-prs/kda-residual-gate-h200-20260927/provenance.json) · [All 40 inclusion/removal decisions](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/blob/42d1d19e5f876e7b5977fb55d90073230bce1655/diffusion-prs/kda-residual-gate-h200-20260927/selection.json)

issues.title: [Diffusion] Enable lossless SANA-Video eager conv fusions for 12.6% lower latency
issues.body:
## Motivation

SANA-Video's frame-batched GLUMB activations are much larger than Sana's image workload. Its native eager profile is more than 99% GPU busy, with **80 convolution-bias additions taking 97.77 ms per complete CFG iteration**, before the separate SiLU and multiply kernels. The existing exact convolution post-processing only runs in BCG contexts.

Reuse those fusions for SANA-Video eager inference. Two native A–B–B–A groups on **one H200** reduce worker E2E by **12.58–12.63%** and client E2E including saved video by **12.54–12.67%**. All lossless output videos remain byte-identical.

## Modifications

- Add an explicit eager opt-in to the shared convolution bias+SiLU and bias+GLU helpers; SANA-Video's GLUMB temporal block opts in. The Sana image default-stream policy stays intact.
- Reuse the existing BF16 rounding boundaries, first-sight exactness checks and permanent fallback on mismatch. Gradient-enabled default-stream calls and compiled/non-CUDA paths keep Torch.
- Keep this dispatch-only change focused on the existing helpers; standalone test and benchmark files are omitted. No new CUDA/Triton arithmetic, LayerNorm policy, approximate attention, sampling or checkpoint change.
- Update the existing SANA-Video fusion-coverage row for eager convolution post-processing.

The implementation reuses #34928 and the SANA-Video wiring in #35961. The image-specific CPU-launch regression discussed in #34015 motivates retaining the original default for image callers. This video profile has a different cost distribution. [Source review and execution flow](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/blob/2e3f75ee1dc52b396e839442803b6952db7ddcd2/diffusion-prs/sana-video-eager-conv-h200/source-review.md).

## Benchmark

`Efficient-Large-Model/SANA-Video_2B_480p_diffusers@db5f398b13ca086d09a50ce156c20527773841b1`, **1× H200**, TP1, native backend, GPU-resident components, BF16 DiT/Gemma2, native FP32 linear-attention accumulation and FP32 latent/VAE policy. Manual performance mode, no torch.compile.

Official video shape: **832×480, 81 frames, 16 fps, 5.0625 s**, 50 requested sampling steps, CFG6, flow shift8, seed42. Fixed 300-token text window and native negative prompt. Prompt: `A curious raccoon walks through a sunlit forest. motion score: 30.` Same-shape warmup at 832×480/81 frames.

Baseline `993d1fccbaafe3e79d91567d2fc1d665cc94fa50`; measured candidate `275113434ffe34412f807514399ba00ef70fa38e`; PR head `64e1e8a92a1942f058b9d6c175f5342198b34709`. Any documentation-only follow-up does not change the measured runtime. Torch2.13.0+cu130, Triton3.7.1, CUDA13.0, driver595.71.05. [Environment](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/blob/2e3f75ee1dc52b396e839442803b6952db7ddcd2/diffusion-prs/sana-video-eager-conv-h200/environment.json).

Fresh native CLI processes on the same idle GPU; A–B–B–A in each group. The eager comparison is repeated twice. BCG runs use actual capture/replay in both arms and provide a regression comparator. Seconds; parentheses show reduction from each group's arithmetic means:

| Group | Worker E2E | Denoise | Client E2E including MP4 save |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| eager-r1 | 44.7324 → 39.1040 (12.58%) | 41.7766 → 36.1501 (13.47%) | 45.210 → 39.480 (12.67%) |
| eager-r2 | 44.7479 → 39.0949 (12.63%) | 41.7929 → 36.1431 (13.52%) | 45.125 → 39.465 (12.54%) |
| bcg-r1 | 37.7962 → 37.7986 (-0.01%) | 34.8571 → 34.8603 (-0.01%) | 38.175 → 38.175 (0.00%) |

<details><summary>All 12 unprofiled native measurements</summary>

| Group | Arm | Worker E2E | Denoise | Client E2E incl. save | Peak reserved GiB |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| eager-r1 | A1 | 44.6694 | 41.7160 | 45.04 | 20.9199 |
| eager-r1 | B1 | 39.0674 | 36.1122 | 39.45 | 21.0176 |
| eager-r1 | B2 | 39.1406 | 36.1880 | 39.51 | 21.0176 |
| eager-r1 | A2 | 44.7954 | 41.8371 | 45.38 | 20.9199 |
| eager-r2 | A1 | 44.7547 | 41.8005 | 45.14 | 20.9199 |
| eager-r2 | B1 | 39.0982 | 36.1451 | 39.47 | 21.0176 |
| eager-r2 | B2 | 39.0916 | 36.1411 | 39.46 | 21.0176 |
| eager-r2 | A2 | 44.7412 | 41.7853 | 45.11 | 20.9199 |
| bcg-r1 | A1 | 37.7978 | 34.8597 | 38.18 | 23.6758 |
| bcg-r1 | B1 | 37.7905 | 34.8525 | 38.16 | 23.6758 |
| bcg-r1 | B2 | 37.8067 | 34.8682 | 38.19 | 23.6758 |
| bcg-r1 | A2 | 37.7946 | 34.8545 | 38.17 | 23.6758 |

</details>

Worker E2E is perf-dump stage duration before saving, excluding loading/warmup. Client E2E is the native scheduler-request/output-save timer, logged to 0.01 s. Profile and benchmark-export timings are excluded. [All raw perf dumps, configs, source SHAs and logs](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/blob/2e3f75ee1dc52b396e839442803b6952db7ddcd2/diffusion-prs/sana-video-eager-conv-h200/raw), [complete evidence](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/blob/2e3f75ee1dc52b396e839442803b6952db7ddcd2/diffusion-prs/sana-video-eager-conv-h200/final-evidence.json).

## Profile and operator benchmark

Each slice contains a complete second positive/negative CFG iteration. CPU third-to-fifth model/graph calls are joined to GPU kernels using CUDA launch correlations. All four slices have zero boundary-crossing GPU kernels. Both BCG profiles contain **eight single-segment graph launches**, with **two in the selected CFG iteration**; no signature miss or eager fallback is accepted.

| Native profile | All kernels | Separate conv post kernels / GPU ms | Fused conv post kernels / GPU ms | Graph launches in slice |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| baseline-eager-profile | 2349 | 200 / 168.9436 | 0 / 0.0000 | 0 |
| baseline-bcg-profile | 2023 | 0 / 0.0000 | 80 / 36.9273 | 2 |
| conv-eager-profile | 2229 | 0 / 0.0000 | 80 / 36.0984 | 0 |
| conv-bcg-profile | 2023 | 0 / 0.0000 | 80 / 36.7944 | 2 |

The fusion removes materialized bias and activation intermediates. Other native operations retain their original implementation. Cumulative device times explain the operators and are not E2E measurements. [Original/sliced traces, source attribution and three-table triage](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/blob/2e3f75ee1dc52b396e839442803b6952db7ddcd2/diffusion-prs/sana-video-eager-conv-h200/profiles).

Committed-wrapper marker benchmark, rotating inputs, median microseconds. These rows include the **actual convolution and post-processing**, with normal output allocation:

| Operation | Native shape | Eager | Fused |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: |
| Pointwise conv + bias + SiLU | [21,2240,30,52] → C13440 | 4459.0695 | 3476.4716 |
| Depthwise conv + bias + GLU | [21,13440,30,52] → C6720 | 3127.3782 | 1174.3818 |

[Raw marker output](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/blob/2e3f75ee1dc52b396e839442803b6952db7ddcd2/diffusion-prs/sana-video-eager-conv-h200/sana-video-conv-marker.log). Output parity is checked separately against the complete native convolution chain, including temporal convolution.

## Output comparison

The audit covers 26 request records. All **22 valid lossless videos**, including unprofiled and profiled eager/BCG runs, are byte-identical. Independent decoding verifies **81/81 identical frames**, SSIM1, PSNR∞, and no audio stream. The before/after contact sheet was visually inspected.

issues.title: [Diffusion] Improve BCG warmup frame-count diagnostics for video models
issues.body:
## Motivation

When breakable CUDA graph (BCG) is enabled for a **video** model without an explicit `--warmup-num-frames`, warmup captures the model's sampling-default frame count (SANA-Video defaults to 81). A serving request with a different frame count then **misses every captured graph** and silently falls back to eager — which is *slower than baseline*, because the mismatched capture was wasted work.

The existing capture-miss hint only mentions `--warmup-resolutions` and never mentions frame count, so a temporal mismatch points the user at the wrong flag.

## Modifications

- Emit a startup log when BCG + a video task runs without `--warmup-num-frames`, stating the default frame count that will be captured, so the mismatch is visible before serving.
- Detect a temporal-only `hidden_states` mismatch (`[B,C,F,H,W]` differing only in `F`) in the capture-miss hint and point at `--warmup-num-frames` instead of only `--warmup-resolutions`. Resolution-only misses keep the original hint.

## Reproduction command

Single B300, SANA-Video `832x480`, **17 frames** (vs the 81-frame sampling default), BCG with resolution declared but **no** `--warmup-num-frames`:

```bash
sglang generate --backend=sglang \
  --model-path Efficient-Large-Model/SANA-Video_2B_480p_diffusers \
  --prompt "A curious raccoon walks through a sunlit forest. motion score: 30." \
  --width 832 --height 480 --num-frames 17 --fps 16 \
  --num-inference-steps 8 --guidance-scale 6.0 --performance-mode manual \
  --num-gpus 1 --seed 42 --quality lossless --warmup-mode request \
  --enable-breakable-cuda-graph --warmup-resolutions 832x480 \
  --save-output
```

## Diagnostic output: before (main) vs after (this PR)

**main** — no startup hint about frame count; the miss hint blames *resolution* and suggests the wrong flag:

```text
[Diffusion BCG] captured 1 segment(s), ... ('hidden_states', ('tensor', (1, 16, 21, 60, 104), 'torch.bfloat16')) ...
[Diffusion BCG] serving signature MISSED 1 captured graph(s); running eager.
[Diffusion BCG]   differing fields (serving vs captured): [('hidden_states', (1, 16, 5, 60, 104), (1, 16, 21, 60, 104))]
[Diffusion BCG] hint: ... declare every served resolution explicitly, e.g. --warmup-resolutions 1024x1024.
```

**this PR** — startup states the captured default frame count, and the miss hint correctly identifies the temporal gap and the right flag:

```text
[Diffusion BCG] --warmup-num-frames unset; capturing the model default warmup frame count (81). Requests with a different frame count run eager. Pass --warmup-num-frames N matching your served frame count.
[Diffusion BCG] serving signature MISSED 1 captured graph(s); running eager.
[Diffusion BCG]   differing fields (serving vs captured): [('hidden_states', (1, 16, 5, 60, 104), (1, 16, 21, 60, 104))]
[Diffusion BCG] hint: the ``hidden_states`` temporal (frame) dimension differs ... declare it explicitly, e.g. --warmup-num-frames 17 (and --warmup-resolutions WxH).
```

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Hardware: one NVIDIA B300. Model: `Efficient-Large-Model/SANA-Video_2B_480p_diffusers`, 832x480, 17 frames, 8 steps.

| Measurement | Denoise | Result |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| Baseline (eager) | 1.24s | — |
| BCG, no `--warmup-num-frames` (the trap) | 1.34s | signature miss → eager, slower than baseline |
| BCG, `--warmup-num-frames 17` (guided fix) | 0.96s | replay, **-22%**, bit-identical output |

With the corrected flag the serving request replays the captured graph and the output is byte-identical to the eager baseline (`md5` match).

## Accuracy Tests

No kernel arithmetic change; this PR only adds/adjusts log lines. The eager fallback output is unchanged, and the correctly-configured BCG run is byte-identical to eager.

## Checklist

- [x] Format the code with pre-commit.
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed results above.
- [x] No user-facing documentation change is required.
- [x] Follow the SGLang code-style guidance.

issues.body:
## Summary

Profile-driven measurements on a **single B300 (275 GB, SM103)** across nine single-GPU-runnable diffusion models (following the `sglang-diffusion-benchmark-profile` skill: fixed seed/prompt/shape, perf dumps + `torch.profiler`, byte-identical / SSIM-PSNR correctness gates).

This documents two findings that change which flags are actually fastest on a large-VRAM single GPU, and fixes two recipe rows.

## Findings

1. **Launch-bound small models gain the most from BCG**
   - SANA1.5-1.6B (image): denoise **0.70s → 0.23s (-67%)**, bit-identical.
   - SANA-Video (832x480, 17 frames): **1.24s → 0.96s (-22%)**, bit-identical.
   - Compute-bound models (LongCat-Image, Qwen-Image, Z-Image, Cosmos3-Edge, FLUX.1-dev, Wan2.1-1.3B) show **no** BCG or `torch.compile` gain — profiles show GEMM + flash-attention + already-fused norm/GELU saturating the device.

2. **Component CPU offload is a pessimization on a 275 GB card**
   - Presets enable `--text-encoder-cpu-offload` for memory-bound cards, but the whole model stays resident, so the H2D/D2H round trip is pure overhead. Dropping it on LingBot-Video-MoE was **8% faster end to end** (3.80s → 3.49s, bit-identical).

## Recipe fixes
- **SANA-Video**: the BCG recipe now includes `--warmup-num-frames 17`. Without it, warmup captures the 81-frame sampling default and a 17-frame request misses the captured graph → falls back to eager, measured **slower than baseline** (1.40s vs 1.24s).
- **LingBot Video MoE**: note that `--text-encoder-cpu-offload` should be dropped on large-VRAM single GPUs.

Docs-only change.

## Summary

- extend the shared diffusion `residual_gate_add` JIT op to the mixed layout used by SANA-Video: a transposed-dense `[B, tokens, hidden]` residual/output, contiguous update, and `[1, 1, hidden]` gate
- use a 32x32 padded shared-memory tile so update reads and residual/output traffic stay coalesced without inserting a full `.contiguous()` copy
- preserve the residual stride and keep all unsupported dtype/layout/device cases on the existing eager fallback
- add production/edge-shape, storage-offset, fullgraph, and CUDA Graph tests; update the registered benchmark and diffusion fast-path documentation

## Motivation

On an NVIDIA H100 80GB profile of native SGLang SANA-Video (832x480x17, 8 steps), the two gated residual sites per transformer block did not reach the existing contiguous-only fusion:

```text
residual shape/stride: [1, 7800, 2240] / (17472000, 1, 7800)
update shape/stride:   [1, 7800, 2240] / (17472000, 2240, 1)
gate shape:            [1, 1, 2240]
```

The lossless 5-step trace attributed 106.1 ms across 720 BF16 add launches to this residual/update shape. Materializing the residual as contiguous would add another full-tensor copy at every site, so this patch handles the mixed layout directly.

## H100 results

Environment: NVIDIA H100 80GB, CUDA 13.0.3, PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130, Triton 3.7.1. Base: `sgl-project/sglang@8eaffdf382e06b7dc50fc5c76cc5aad9c36bb0e4`.

| SANA-Video `[1, 7800, 2240]` mixed layout | 195.83 us | 85.47 us | 2.291x |
